title: bro_exec with NFS-resident cwd wedges in session-start doc-tree read (open(2) never returns)
wanted_capability: Dispatch to lane checkouts (the documented PROJECT.md pattern: claim lane, pass path as dispatch cwd) must not wedge. Observed 2026-07-19 on the prod daemon (started Jul 18 03:24): every bro_exec with cwd under /Users/invidious/lanes/* stalled forever before session_start; stacks show UserInstructions::from_project -> read_doc_tree -> read_to_string -> open(2) blocked indefinitely on NFS regular files, while metadata syscalls on the same tree succeed and non-daemon processes open the same files in 3ms. Non-lane cwd dispatch is unaffected. A prod daemon restart likely clears it (operator-gated; not attempted). Two independent fixes worth doing regardless: (1) bound the doc-tree read with a timeout and degrade to no-overlay with a warning instead of hanging session start; (2) investigate the NFS client state that lets a long-lived launchd daemon wedge on open(2) while other processes succeed.
missing_primitive: either a bounded/timeout doc-tree read (any startup fs read that can hang should have a deadline and fail open with a warning), or a daemon-side fix for the wedged NFS client state, or session startup that defers doc-tree reads off the critical path
fallback_used: Dispatch with local-disk cwd (git worktrees under .claude/worktrees), rsync worktree into a claimed lane for pod-routed cargo gates.
evidence: sample stacks: 6 threads in bro_harness::project_doc::read_doc_tree -> read_to_string -> __open (never returns)
fs_usage: getattrlist/lstat/statfs on the same NFS tree succeed in microseconds for the daemon
pong probes 2026-07-19: lane cwd (bpool4) stalled x3, main-repo cwd completed in seconds x1
mounts: auto_lanes autofs + per-lane NFS from 192.168.0.16x workers, healthy for all other processes
